raw_response:
I am old already, so this year I will not do anything too fancy. I still farm the way I know from many years. Wheat and maize go together on most of my land because that gives steady grain and cash, and if one side is not good, the other still helps. Cotton takes more picking work, so I will keep less of it because there are only two of us at home. I have a well, but pumping costs money, so I will use water at the key times, not too many times. Fertilizer also costs a lot now. I would rather not cut too much, because if wheat or maize turns yellow, yield drops fast. So I will do about the same as the years when the harvest was decent: wheat a bit heavier, maize moderate, cotton less area and not too much input. I do what fits my hands and my pocket, not what sounds best on paper.
